analysis: INH (isoniazid) is an antibiotic used primarily for the treatment of tuberculosis. It is known to interfere with the metabolism of pyridoxine (vitamin B6), leading to a deficiency that can result in peripheral neuropathy. The standard medical treatment for INH-induced neuropathy is supplementation with pyridoxine. This is because pyridoxine supplementation can prevent or reverse the neuropathy caused by isoniazid. The enhanced information supports this consensus, indicating that pyridoxine is the correct treatment for INH-induced neuropathy. Other options such as thiamine, niacin, and riboflavin are not relevant to the specific mechanism of INH-induced neuropathy.
